thesis: This episode argues that Qualcomm (QCOM) is well-positioned for growth driven by its structural tailwinds in the Internet of Things, edge computing, and automotive sectors, following a strategic shift under new CEO Cristiano Amman. It highlights Qualcomm's strong relationships with major customers like Apple and Meta, its dominance in high-end smartphones, and its successful selective bolt-on acquisitions like Nuvia. The thesis also notes that while Qualcomm faces some exceptions like Apple for AR/VR, it is moving into new areas like AR, VR, and automotive, and has a clear direction and focus on its sweet spots.

claims.quote: And what Qualcomm really did, what really drove its rise to prominence, was its ability to work with the organization that sets the wireless standards. It's a UN agency. And Qualcomm worked that group, managed it, invested heavily in the R&D, so that by the time we got to 3G, a lot of what Qualcomm had done for their CDMA standards, got incorporated into the global GSTM standard for 3G.
